review_notes: I read the whole file and compared it with sibling files in the same library: DenseOpenRationalCategoryOver, IntegralDominantRationalCategory and the client tests. The existing simp lemmas toRationalMap_hom, toRationalMap_id, toRationalMap_comp and homEquivDominant_apply_val are fine in direction and do not conflict. I did not recommend rewriting compOfPullsDenseOpens to comp, because compOfPullsDenseOpens_eq_comp needs dominance and preirreducibility hypotheses that the general category lacks. I did not run Lean, so I have not checked that the proposed lemmas compile or that simp currently fails on the stated goals. The first finding is the more solid one, since a sibling already has the corresponding lemma. The second is a smaller completeness gap.

findings.problem: `of` is an ordinary (non-reducible) def with no accompanying simp lemma for its projection. A term like `(DenseOpenRationalScheme.of X).toScheme` is therefore not normalised to `X` by `simp`, and it appears in the types of `Hom`, `toRationalMap_id` and similar. The sibling `DenseOpenRationalSchemeOver.of` has `@[simp] toScheme_of`, so the interface is inconsistent. `IntegralDenseOpenRationalScheme.of` is built from this `of`, and the client test proves `(IntegralDenseOpenRationalScheme.of X).obj.toScheme = X := rfl` by hand.
findings.proposed_change: Add right after `of`: `@[simp] theorem toScheme_of (X : Scheme.{u}) : (of X).toScheme = X := rfl`.
findings.benefit: Downstream `simp` calls reduce `(of X).toScheme` to `X` automatically. Rational-map statements about `of X ⟶ of Y` then simplify to statements about `X ⤏ Y` without manual `show` or `rfl` steps. This also matches the sibling convention.

evidence.excerpt:
@[simp] theorem toScheme_of {S X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ S) :
    (of p).toScheme = X := rfl

findings.problem: `homEquivDominant` is a def built with `Equiv` and has a simp lemma only for the forward direction. The inverse direction `(homEquivDominant X Y).symm r` has no simp lemma. `simp` cannot expose its underlying rational map, which is `r.1`, and cannot reduce `hom r.1 _`. Round trips such as `(homEquivDominant X Y).symm r` followed by `toRationalMap` therefore need manual unfolding, even though the two simp lemmas `toRationalMap_hom` and `homEquivDominant_apply_val` already cover the other cases.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem homEquivDominant_symm_apply_toRationalMap (X Y : DenseOpenRationalScheme.{u}) [PreirreducibleSpace X.toScheme] [Nonempty X.toScheme] [PreirreducibleSpace Y.toScheme] [Nonempty Y.toScheme] (r : {r : X.toScheme ⤏ Y.toScheme // r.IsDominant}) : ((homEquivDominant X Y).symm r).toRationalMap = r.1 := rfl`. Giving `homEquivDominant_apply_val` a name that matches the `Equiv` apply/symm_apply convention would also help.
findings.benefit: Both directions of the equivalence then simplify to the underlying rational map. Users can transport dominant rational maps into the category and read them back out with `simp` instead of unfolding the definition.

    ((Scheme.RationalMap.pullsDenseOpens_iff_isDominant r.1).mpr r.2)
